plain: To invent or work out a plan or method

webster.text: To invent; to contrive; to form in the mind by new combinations of ideas, new applications of principles, or new arrangement of parts; to excogitate; to strike out by thought; to plan; to scheme; to project; as, to devise an engine or machine; to devise a new mode of writing; to devise a plan of defense; to devise arguments.

more.text: To consider; to contrive; to lay a plan; to form a scheme.

example.quote: It seemed peculiarly desireable therefore that some other mode of election should be devised.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 6, 1787
